title: Seathan born to the keeper's hearth
summary: Seathan is born at Tobar dhìreach, the only son of the keeper of the fire coal and the rainbow, and has the fire coal in his hands from earliest childhood as every child of that hearth has had it before him.

title: Seathan takes the bag over
summary: On his father's death Seathan takes the bag of two coals and the keeping in his thirty-second year, and chooses, unlike his father before him, to keep the fire coal near the hearth rather than carry it abroad.

title: Seathan marries Caitir
summary: Seathan takes Caitir, of a household two valleys east that keeps no coal of its own, and she comes to Tobar dhìreach knowing she marries a keeper and not only a husband.

title: The fire coal put into the pot itself
summary: Seathan puts the fire coal into the fire the line holds to be the mason's own, carried unbroken since the night of the lightning, and it lies dark and cool through the flame as it lies in every other fire he has tried.

title: Seathan snaps his fingers on the doorstone
summary: On a warm evening Seathan, breaking the fire coal into dust between his fingers and thinking of the mason and the lightning's crack, snaps his fingers without meaning to try anything, and the dust on his hand takes fire, red-gold, and leaves no mark on him.

title: Seathan laughs until Caitir comes
summary: Seathan sits on the doorstone laughing until his wife comes out to him, and tells her, before he tells anyone else, that the fire has been in his own hand the whole thirty years he carried it.

title: The telling at the hearth
summary: Seathan tells the fire coal's waking at the recital on the night of the lightning that same year, plainly, as he told it to Caitir, and the valley begins to call the sixth coal gual teine, the fire coal.

title: The rainbow thrown into the northern sea again
summary: Seathan carries the rainbow coal to the northern shore in the old custom and throws it into the swell, and wades in after it to find it as dark and salt-wet as it went in.

title: The rainbow tried at the river crossing
summary: Seathan and Caitir carry the rainbow coal down to the crossing where the silver still burns under the current, and hold it and then throw it, and it lies cold and ordinary among the wet stones the next morning.

title: Caitir's saying of the rainbow
summary: Caitir says, after the river trial, that the rainbow holds every spirit and so belongs wholly to none of them, a saying that afterward passes among Clann na Ceiste.

title: Seathan dies at his own hearth
summary: Seathan dies in his three-and-seventieth year at Tobar dhìreach, the fire-pot burning near him, asking at the last to hold the fire coal once more rather than the rainbow.

title: The bag passes to a son-in-law
summary: The bag, holding only the rainbow now, passes from Seathan's grave to his eldest daughter's husband, a man of a neighbouring hearth married into the keeping.

title: Caitir tries the rainbow once more
summary: Caitir, staying on at Tobar dhìreach after Seathan's death, tries the rainbow once more at the river for the comfort of doing something with it, and it lies as dark and unmoved as it lay in her husband's hand.

title: Caitir dies at Tobar dhìreach
summary: Caitir dies in her three-and-seventieth year, the same age Seathan reached before her, and is buried beside him near the slab.
